summary: Exact R(2^k−1) for all k ≤ 61 via a dedicated divisor search (for u ≤ v put w = 4Cu−1 = (n+u)/v, sieve-factor n+u for u ≤ √n/2; ~25 CPU-min total; matches the 1e8 census for k ≤ 26 and an independent sympy check R(2^33−1) = 44): R = 0 exactly at k ∈ {2,3,4,5,7,8,13} and R > 0 for every 14 ≤ k ≤ 61 (CERTIFIED; e.g. R = 228 at k = 61, minimum over 30 ≤ k ≤ 61 is 22 at k = 31). Mechanism (PROVED, elementary): no (★) solution n = 4Cuv−u−v of a Mersenne n has u or v in B_k = {1,2} ∪ {2^i+1 : i ≡ k (mod 2)}, because then the needed divisor w ≡ −1 (mod 4u) of n+u is an odd divisor of 2^k, of 2^k+1 (prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4, or ≡ 1,3 mod 8 for k odd) or of 2^{k−i}+1 with k−i even (all odd divisors ≡ 1 mod 4). Residue-matched controls n = 2^k−1+840j (200 per k ≤ 44, 40 per k ≤ 50) get 23% of R from min(u,v) ∈ B_k, and Mersenne R averages 0.70 × the control mean (k = 14..50; median percentile 0.18), so the zeros are this structural ~25–30% depletion plus small-n fluctuation (control means ≈ 9–14 at k ≤ 13), not a persistent obstruction.
not_done: The residual depletion beyond B_k (0.70 observed vs ≈0.77 predicted) is not explained; controls count only min(u,v) ∈ B_k, so the B_k share is a slight undercount; k > 61 not run.
next: Only if wanted: split R(2^k−1) by u to find the remaining structurally depleted u-classes (e.g. u with u−1 = 2^i·s, small s).

summary: The first step (U, R, Uv at 8 803 369) was already done in Pass 1 (U = 140, R = 16, I3 = 68, Uv = 11: not an R-zero or U-failure). Here a residue-matched control was added: among 40 primes ≡ 8 803 369 (mod 840) within ±1.1·10⁵, U ranges 131–366 (median 248) and only one has U < 140, so the greedy-record prime is U-hard (2nd lowest of 41) but not extreme. An independent C scan of v(p) = 4x(p) − p over all 4 904 759 399 primes < 1.2·10¹¹ (exact divisor-pair criterion: m/(px) is a sum of two unit fractions iff two divisors of px sum to 0 mod m; Pollard-rho factoring) reproduces A400619/A400620 exactly through the 9th term: records (p, v) = …, (118801, 59), (8 803 369, 107), (119 945 383 009, 111); the only other prime with v ≥ 100 is 45 195 081 409 (v = 103), CERTIFIED. The (★) count at the 9th term is R(119 945 383 009) = 56 (exact divisor search, scripts/z52d_p2_ZF0_Z0759_Rmersenne.c), so it is not an R-zero either.
not_done: U(119 945 383 009) itself (the linear count program needs ≈15 CPU-h at 1.2·10¹¹; no faster exact U counter written); Uv/I3 at the 9th term. The 1.2·10¹¹ scan took ≈37 min wall on 4 cores on an overloaded machine (load ≈ 37/24), slightly over the 30-min cap.
next: If U at the 9th term matters, write a Type-I/Type-II parametrised U counter (ET coordinates) instead of the per-x counter.

summary: Ranked all 6 587 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 360360) below 10¹⁰ by a truncated Euler product L(1,χ_p) (q ≤ 3·10⁵; 22 s): lcm(1..19)+1 = 232 792 561 has L = 6.11, the 90th percentile; the maximum is L = 7.13 at 5 843 237 401. Exact U (count program) for the 8 lowest-L and 8 highest-L class members ≤ 1.5·10⁸ (≈27 CPU-min) gives U/log³p = 0.054–0.063 for L ≈ 3.75–4.50 and 0.038–0.054 for L ≈ 5.97–6.32 (Spearman(L, U/log³p) = −0.77 over 17 primes incl. lcm19+1; log-log slope −0.77). So inside its class lcm(1..19)+1 (0.0386) is typical for its L: three of the high-L primes near 1.4·10⁸ are as low (0.0381–0.0394). Extrapolating the slope, the L-maximal prime < 10¹⁰ would sit only ≈ 12 % lower (≈ 0.034), i.e. L(1,χ_p) moves U by tens of percent, not orders of magnitude (EVIDENCE).
not_done: U for the L-extreme primes between 1.5·10⁸ and 10¹⁰ (the per-x count program needs ~3n ints of memory and ~n^1.07 time: ≈2 h and >8 GB at 5.8·10⁹); no out-of-class controls at the same height (all 17 primes share p ≡ 1 mod 360360).
next: A faster parametrised U counter (ET Type I/II coordinates) would allow U at the L-maximal prime 5 843 237 401.

summary: The CUDA port cannot be built or benchmarked here: the machine has only an AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (no CUDA/nvcc; Vulkan only). Instead the census kernel itself was benchmarked and accelerated on CPU: levels C = 1, 2, 3 are decided by a segmented sieve, since (ℤ/4C)^* has exponent 2 for 4C | 24, so −1 is a divisor residue of 4Cp+1 iff it lies in the subgroup generated by its prime factors' residues (PROVED, elementary); only the ≈2.3 % of primes unresolved at C ≤ 3 fall back to trial division. On 2·10⁷-wide windows at 10¹⁰, 10¹¹, 10¹² the per-prime Cmin output is byte-identical to scripts/z52d_p2_SK2_cmin_seg.c and 3.1×, 4.9×, 5.0× faster (1.3/1.9/3.1 s vs 4.2/9.2/15.5 s). With it the C-form census was extended from 10¹⁰ to 5·10¹⁰ (832 298 890 primes ≡ 1 mod 4, 53 CPU-min): every prime has a certificate (CERTIFIED), Cmin = 1 for 81.7 %, and the only prime with Cmin > 3000 is 35 848 375 369 (Cmin = 3632, u = 33, B = 74 774, verified; R = 12).
not_done: No GPU kernel was written or benchmarked (no CUDA device). The census beyond 5·10¹⁰ was not run: the sieve version projects to ≈35 CPU-h for 10¹⁰–10¹², which is beyond the cap, and the trial-division fallback still dominates its cost.
next: Extend the sieve to the non-exponent-2 levels C = 4, 5 (by storing factor lists rather than residue masks); that removes most of the fallback cost and should bring 10¹² within a few CPU-h, without a GPU.

summary: Wrote the segmented word sieve (windows [A,A+W); each pair (t,u) visited once per window with v ≥ u and v restricted by n ≡ 1 mod 4; ordered I3/R/Uv rebuilt from both orders; uint16 counters, 0 saturations). It matches scripts/z52b_fingerprint_words.c exactly on all 74 416 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4) ≤ 2·10⁶ across 7 windows. Ran: complete per-n counts for all primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4) < 5·10⁹, plus the window [10¹⁰, 1.05·10¹⁰) (2.26·10¹¹ triples, ≈2 CPU-h). Zeros: R = 0 only at the 14 known primes ≤ 8 813 281 (I3 = 0 only at 5, 13, 17; Uv never 0) (CERTIFIED). The per-dyadic minima rise slowly: min R = 2, 6, 10 (partial bin) on 2^30, 2^31, 2^32 and 12 on the 10¹⁰ window, against medians 70/74/76/82; min I3 = 90 → 108 and min Uv = 17 → 38 on the same bins (data/z52b/pass2/ZF0/Z0779/summary.json).
not_done: [5·10⁹, 10¹⁰) is not run: at the measured rate that is ≈170 CPU-min, about 45 min wall on 4 cores, which is over the cap. The 10¹⁰ height is sampled by one 5·10⁸ window only. Per-n counts are not exported (≈700 MB); only histograms and zeros are kept.
next: Run the remaining [5·10⁹, 10¹⁰) windows with the same binary (4 procs, W=5·10⁸) if the complete range is needed.
